name: Potassium chloride
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Potassium chloride treats or prevents hypokalemia. The kidneys excrete potassium, so kidney impairment sharply raises the risk of hyperkalemia. The US label (oral extended-release tablets) starts patients with kidney impairment at the low end of the dose range and asks for frequent potassium checks; it is contraindicated with triamterene or amiloride.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses 'renal impairment' without a number; dose is titrated to serum potassium.
chip: CKD: start low; frequent K checks

bands.recommendation: Hypokalemia treatment: 40 to 100 mEq/day in divided doses, no more than 40 mEq per dose; prevention: about 20 mEq/day. Use IV potassium if serum potassium is below 2.5 mEq/L (label).

Reduced potassium excretion and a much higher risk of hyperkalemia: start at the low end of the dose range, especially with RAAS inhibitors or NSAIDs; monitor serum potassium frequently and kidney function periodically (label 8.7).

hd: No dialysis dose in label; potassium removal depends on the dialysate. Give only for documented hypokalemia, start low and check potassium frequently (label 8.7); specialist input.
pd: No PD dose in label. PD patients can become hypokalemic; replace by measured potassium, starting low (label 8.7); specialist input.
crrt: No data in label; replacement guided by frequent potassium levels and CRRT fluid potassium. Specialist input.
dialyzable: Potassium is removed by hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis (label lists dialysis among hyperkalemia treatments).
monitoring: Serum potassium frequently in kidney impairment and periodically on maintenance; kidney function; magnesium, acid-base status and ECG in cardiac or kidney disease (label 2.1, 8.7).

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and effectiveness in children not established (oral extended-release tablets; label).

adult: Label covers oral extended-release tablets (600 mg = 8 mEq; 750 mg = 10 mEq), matching PH tablets. PH also registers 2 mEq/mL IV concentrate (20 products), which must be diluted; IV rate and concentration limits are not in this label. Consider adding an IV label as an alternate.
